overview.title: The chapter 8 ConvNet's summary and preprocessing a test image (listing 10.1)
overview.main_topic: The remaining layers and parameter totals of the reloaded dogs-vs-cats ConvNet, and listing 10.1, which downloads a cat image and turns it into a (1, 180, 180, 3) batch tensor
overview.central_idea: The model being inspected is a stack of five Conv2D layers (32→512 filters) interleaved with four MaxPooling2D layers, followed by global average pooling, dropout and a 1-unit Dense layer: 1,569,089 trainable parameters. To visualize its activations you need one input image the network has never seen, loaded at the training resolution and wrapped as a batch of one sample.
overview.importance: Knowing each layer's output shape tells you what the activation maps you are about to plot will look like (e.g. 89×89×32 after the first pooling, 7×7×512 at the last conv). The preprocessing helper `get_img_array` is reused later in the chapter.

summary:
The page continues the `model.summary()` table from p.309 for the ConvNet trained from scratch with data augmentation in chapter 8. After `conv2d_11` (178×178×32), the layers are:

| layer | output shape | params |
|---|---|---|
| max_pooling2d_6 | (None, 89, 89, 32) | 0 |
| conv2d_12 | (None, 87, 87, 64) | 18,496 |
| max_pooling2d_7 | (None, 43, 43, 64) | 0 |
| conv2d_13 | (None, 41, 41, 128) | 73,856 |
| max_pooling2d_8 | (None, 20, 20, 128) | 0 |
| conv2d_14 | (None, 18, 18, 256) | 295,168 |
| max_pooling2d_9 | (None, 9, 9, 256) | 0 |
| conv2d_15 | (None, 7, 7, 512) | 1,180,160 |
| global_average_pooling2d_3 | (None, 512) | 0 |
| dropout | (None, 512) | 0 |
| dense_3 | (None, 1) | 513 |

The totals are **Total params: 4,707,269 (17.96 MB)**, **Trainable params: 1,569,089 (5.99 MB)**, **Non-trainable params: 0** and **Optimizer params: 3,138,180 (11.97 MB)**. The trainable count is the 1,569,089 that p.306 compares against the mini Xception model.

Next you need an input image: **a picture of a cat that was not part of the training images**. **Listing 10.1** downloads `cat.jpg` with `keras.utils.get_file` and defines `get_img_array(img_path, target_size)`, which:
1. opens the file and resizes it with `keras.utils.load_img(..., target_size=target_size)`,
2. turns it into a float32 NumPy array of shape (180, 180, 3) with `keras.utils.img_to_array`,
3. adds a leading axis with `np.expand_dims(array, axis=0)` to make a "batch" of a single sample, of shape **(1, 180, 180, 3)**.

It is called with `target_size=(180, 180)` to produce `img_tensor`, the input used for all activation plots in section 10.1.

concepts.name: Keras model summary
concepts.definition: A table of a model's layers with output shapes and parameter counts, plus totals.
concepts.intuition: A blueprint of the network you are about to probe.
concepts.technical: Total params = trainable + non-trainable + optimizer params. Here 1,569,089 + 0 + 3,138,180 = 4,707,269. Sizes in MB assume 4 bytes per float32 value (1,569,089 × 4 B ≈ 5.99 MB).
concepts.significance: Tells you which layers produce which feature-map shapes, i.e. what you will visualize.
concepts.misconception: That 'Total params' is the model's learnable size. Here it includes 3,138,180 optimizer variables saved with the model; only 1,569,089 are trainable weights.

concepts.name: Max pooling
concepts.definition: Downsampling by taking the maximum over windows, here 2×2 with stride 2.
concepts.intuition: Keep the strongest response in each neighbourhood and halve the resolution.
concepts.significance: It shrinks feature maps so that deeper layers see larger regions of the image.
concepts.example: An 87×87 map becomes 43×43 (the odd last row/column is dropped).
concepts.misconception: That pooling has weights. Param # is 0.

concepts.name: Batch axis
concepts.definition: The leading dimension of a model input that indexes samples.
concepts.intuition: Models always expect a pile of images, even if the pile has one image.
concepts.technical: `np.expand_dims(array, axis=0)` turns (180, 180, 3) into (1, 180, 180, 3), matching the model's (None, 180, 180, 3) input.
concepts.significance: Without it, the model would misinterpret the array's axes or raise a shape error.
concepts.misconception: That a single image can be passed with shape (180, 180, 3).

concepts.name: Single-image preprocessing
concepts.definition: Loading an image file, resizing it to the model's input size, converting to a float array and adding a batch axis.
concepts.intuition: Put the image into exactly the format the network was trained on.
concepts.technical: load_img(target_size) → img_to_array (float32) → expand_dims. Pixel rescaling is not done here because the model contains a Rescaling layer (p.309).
concepts.significance: The input must match the training preprocessing, or the activations will not reflect normal model behaviour.
concepts.misconception: That you must divide by 255 before feeding this model; its built-in Rescaling layer does that.

math.title: Spatial sizes through the conv/pool stack

variables.meaning: Height (= width) of the feature map entering the layer

math.operations: Alternating subtraction of 2 (each 3×3 valid convolution) and halving with rounding down (each pooling layer).
math.purpose: Explains every output shape in the printed summary.
math.interpretation: Resolution drops from 180 to 7 while depth grows from 3 to 512: the typical ConvNet trade of spatial detail for feature richness.
math.intuition: Each block makes the maps smaller and the stack of maps thicker.

math.title: Conv2D parameter counts and the trainable total

variables.meaning: Parameters of one Conv2D layer (weights + biases)

math.operations: Multiply kernel area by input and output channels, add one bias per filter; sum over layers. Dense: 512 inputs × 1 + 1 bias.
math.purpose: Reproduces the Param # column and the trainable total.
math.interpretation: The last conv layer alone has 1,180,160 parameters, about 75% of the model: parameters concentrate where channel counts are largest.
math.intuition: Doubling both input and output channels quadruples a layer's parameters.

math.title: Total parameters and memory
math.source_text: Total params: 4,707,269 (17.96 MB) Trainable params: 1,569,089 (5.99 MB) Non-trainable params: 0 (0.00 B) Optimizer params: 3,138,180 (11.97 MB)
math.operations: Sum of the three categories; memory = count × 4 bytes ÷ 1024².
math.purpose: Explains how the summary's totals and sizes relate.
math.interpretation: Optimizer params are almost exactly 2× the trainable params (2 × 1,569,089 = 3,138,178, plus 2). Beyond the book: this matches an optimizer such as Adam keeping two moment estimates per weight plus a couple of scalar state variables; the book does not say which.
math.intuition: A saved, trained model carries the optimizer's memory, which here is twice the size of the weights.

line_explanations.explanation: Four rounds of MaxPooling2D (halving the spatial size) and Conv2D (shrinking by 2 and increasing filters 64→128→256→512). Pooling layers have 0 parameters; conv parameters follow 3·3·C_in·C_out + C_out.
Head: GlobalAveragePooling2D reduces 7×7×512 to a 512-vector, Dropout keeps the shape, Dense(1) has 512 + 1 = 513 parameters.
Totals: 1,569,089 trainable weights, no non-trainable ones (no batch normalization in this model), and 3,138,180 optimizer variables saved with the model.

code.inputs_outputs: No inputs; it is a description of the model. Shapes include the batch axis as None.
code.theory_link: Each Conv2D and MaxPooling2D row is a layer whose activation will be visualized (listing 10.3 on p.311 picks exactly these layer types).
pitfalls: Layer name suffixes (_6, _12, _3) depend on your session and will differ.
Do not confuse Total params with model capacity; it includes optimizer state.

code.title: Preprocessing a single image
code.original_code:
import keras
import numpy as np
img_path = keras.utils.get_file(
    fname="cat.jpg", origin="https://img-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/cat.jpg"
)
def get_img_array(img_path, target_size):
    img = keras.utils.load_img(img_path, target_size=target_size)
    array = keras.utils.img_to_array(img)
    array = np.expand_dims(array, axis=0)
    return array
img_tensor = get_img_array(img_path, target_size=(180, 180))
code.what_it_does: Downloads a test cat image and converts it into a float32 NumPy batch of shape (1, 180, 180, 3) suitable as input to the chapter 8 ConvNet.

line_explanations.explanation: `keras.utils.get_file` downloads cat.jpg from the given URL (callout: "Downloads a test image"), caches it locally and returns the local path.
`get_img_array` opens the file and resizes it to `target_size` with `keras.utils.load_img`, which returns a PIL image (callout: "Opens the image file and resizes it").
`img_to_array` turns the image into a float32 NumPy array of shape (180, 180, 3) (callout).
`np.expand_dims(array, axis=0)` adds a batch dimension: "a 'batch' of a single sample. Its shape is now (1, 180, 180, 3)" (callout).
Return the batch, and call the function with the model's input size (180, 180) to produce `img_tensor`.

code.inputs_outputs: Input: a URL / file path and a target size. Output: `img_tensor`, a float32 array of shape (1, 180, 180, 3) with pixel values in 0–255.
code.algorithm: Download → load and resize → to float array → add batch axis.
code.theory_link: Models process batches; the input shape must match the model's (None, 180, 180, 3). Pixel scaling to [0, 1] is handled by the model's own Rescaling layer.

parameters.name: fname
parameters.role: Local filename for the cached download.

parameters.name: target_size
parameters.role: (height, width) to resize to; must be (180, 180) for this model.

parameters.name: axis=0
parameters.role: Position of the new batch axis.

pitfalls: Forgetting `expand_dims` gives a (180, 180, 3) array that the model cannot take as a batch.
Using a different target_size would produce activations of different shapes and may not match the trained model's expected input.
Resizing with `target_size` does not preserve aspect ratio; the image can be distorted.
code.illustrative_code:

print(img_tensor.min(), img_tensor.max())  # within 0..255

deeper.title: What the activation maps will look like, layer by layer
deeper.body:
From the summary, the activations you will plot in section 10.1 are:

- conv2d_11: 32 maps of 178×178, then pooled to 89×89
- conv2d_12: 64 maps of 87×87, then 43×43
- conv2d_13: 128 maps of 41×41, then 20×20
- conv2d_14: 256 maps of 18×18, then 9×9
- conv2d_15: 512 maps of 7×7

The first layers have high resolution and few channels, so they look image-like. The deep layers are tiny (7×7) but numerous, and p.314 notes they are more abstract and sparser.

deeper.title: Why the training-time model includes optimizer parameters
deeper.body: A `.keras` file saved after training stores the optimizer's state so training can resume exactly where it stopped. Adaptive optimizers keep per-weight statistics. The printed 3,138,180 is 2 × 1,569,089 + 2, consistent with two slots per weight plus two scalars (e.g. iteration count and learning rate). This is an inference: the page shows the number but does not explain it. For inference and visualization, the optimizer state is irrelevant.

takeaways: The chapter 8 ConvNet alternates five Conv2D layers (32→512 filters) and four MaxPooling2D layers, shrinking 180×180 to 7×7 while depth grows to 512.
Every Param # can be reproduced as 3·3·C_in·C_out + C_out; the total of 1,569,089 trainable parameters matches p.306.
Total params (4,707,269) include 3,138,180 optimizer variables; there are no non-trainable params.
Listing 10.1 downloads an unseen cat image, resizes it to 180×180, converts it to float32 and adds a batch axis: shape (1, 180, 180, 3).
No manual pixel scaling is needed because the model contains its own Rescaling layer.

questions.question: Verify the 73,856 parameters of conv2d_13.
questions.explanation: conv2d_13 takes 64 input channels (from conv2d_12/pooling) and has 128 filters of size 3×3, each with a bias.

questions.question: Why is the output of max_pooling2d_7 43×43 rather than 43.5×43.5?
options: Pooling with size 2, stride 2 rounds down: floor(87/2) = 43
questions.answer: Pooling with size 2, stride 2 rounds down: floor(87/2) = 43
questions.explanation: With valid pooling, only complete windows count; 87 allows 43 full 2×2 windows. 'same' padding would give 44; the conv shrink already happened (89→87); Dropout never changes shapes.

questions.question: What does `np.expand_dims(array, axis=0)` do in listing 10.1, and why is it needed?
questions.answer: It adds a leading batch axis, turning (180, 180, 3) into (1, 180, 180, 3), because the model expects batches of images.
questions.explanation: The callout says it makes a 'batch' of a single sample.

questions.question: Why use a cat picture that was not part of the training images?
questions.answer: To see how the trained network processes new, unseen data, its normal operating condition, rather than an image it may have memorized.
questions.explanation: The page specifies the image is not from the training set; interpreting the model on unseen data reflects how it generalizes.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the summary's totals?
questions.explanation: 1,569,089 + 0 + 3,138,180 = 4,707,269. 'Trainable × 3' is off by 2; non-trainable alone would give 1,569,089; optimizer params are about twice the trainable count.

questions.question: Which layer holds the most parameters, and roughly what fraction of the trainable total?
questions.explanation: Its channel counts (256 in, 512 out) are the largest, and conv parameters scale with C_in × C_out.

questions.question: Can you predict the shape of the activation you'd get from max_pooling2d_8 for img_tensor?
questions.explanation: The summary shows (None, 20, 20, 128); for a batch of one, None becomes 1.
